title: Two Ways to Talk About Tomorrow

sections.title: It's not about how soon — it's about how certain
sections.content: You already know present tense plus a future time word: Holnap dolgozom ("Tomorrow I work/I'm working"). That's still exactly right for something near-certain and already arranged — your regular schedule, a fixed appointment. fog + infinitive is for the OTHER kind of future statement: a genuine prediction, an intention, or a promise — something you're saying will happen, not something already fixed on your calendar. holnap can introduce either one; the construction you pick is what signals which kind of future you mean.

items.english: Tomorrow I'm working. (my regular schedule — already fixed)
Tomorrow I'll definitely work a lot. (a prediction about how the day will go)

items.spanish: Holnapután valószínűleg fogok pihenni egy kicsit.
items.english: The day after tomorrow I'll probably rest a little. (not fixed, just an expectation)

sections.content: If you could put it straight into your calendar as-is, reach for the present tense you already know. If it's a guess, a hope, or a promise about what will happen, fog + infinitive is the natural choice — that's exactly why words like biztosan and valószínűleg show up next to it so often.
